name: Learn basic finger drumming
blurb: Drum patterns played on pads or a keyboard. It teaches real rhythmic feel with none of the noise, space or expense of a kit.
gear: A pad controller, or a keyboard with drum sounds, or even a phone app
steps: Learn the standard layout: kick, snare, closed hat, open hat on four pads you can reach comfortably.
Learn the basic backbeat: kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, hats on every eighth note.
Play it to a metronome at 80 bpm until it is effortless, then vary the tempo.
Add variations: kick on the off-beat, open hat on the and of 4, ghost notes on the snare.
Learn a second genre pattern — a hip-hop pattern or a four-on-the-floor house beat.
Play a full two-minute groove with fills every eight bars, without drifting from the click.
tips: Velocity sensitivity is what separates a groove from a drum-machine pattern. Vary how hard you hit.
Practise with the metronome on beats 2 and 4 only — it exposes timing you did not know was loose.
proof: A two-minute live groove with fills, locked to a click, recorded in one take.
